sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Hill (1942) treats the species described by Brauer in 1865 from New South Wales specimens as the typical subspecies, Rhinotermes (Schedorhinotermes) intermedius intermedius, with the type locality Sydney. The alate is yellow ochraceous above, with a hyaline wing membrane and a markedly inflated postclypeus; the soldier occurs in a large and a small form, the large one with a large head, broadly rounded behind and at the sides, widest at about the posterior third, antennal segment 4 the shortest, and the right mandible without a short tooth between the base and the large tooth.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Yellow ochraceous above, the antennae, maxillary palpi, postclypeus and venter slightly paler, the radius and radial sector yellowish brown, the wing membrane hyaline. Frons depressed and grooved. Compound eyes large. Ocelli large, broadly oval, very close to the compound eyes. Postclypeus markedly inflated, not prolonged anteriorly. The anterior and posterior margins of the pronotum slightly wavy. The posterior margin of the mesonotum broadly and shallowly concave. The fore wing bud covers the basal half of the hind wing bud. Measurements: length with wings 17.00—18.00 (the original OCR reads "17-00 - 18.00"); length without wings 8.00—8.50; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.75—1.87; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.13—1.34; head width 1.72—1.75; maximum diameter of compound eye 0.47—0.55; ocellus length 0.14—0.18; pronotum length OCRed in the original as "O.BC - 0.92", of which only the second value is legible; pronotum width 1.46—1.66; fore wing length 13.50—14.00; fore wing width 4.00—4.25.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Large form: head pale yellow, slightly darker than the rest of the body, the base of the mandibles yellowish brown, the distal half pale rusty. Head (Fig. 92) large, broadly rounded behind and at the sides, widest at about the posterior third, narrowing forwards to the base of the mandibles, with hairs from very few to rather numerous. The apices of the mandibles evenly incurved; the right mandible without a short tooth between the base and the large tooth. Labrum slightly longer than wide, broadly bilobed in front. Antennae 18-segmented; segment 3 almost always longer than segment 2; segment 4 the shortest. Pronotum short and broad, the anterior margin convex and folded upwards in the middle, with or without a median notch; the posterior margin wavy or concave. Small form: colour as in the large form; head (Fig. 93) with parallel sides, very rarely slightly wider in front, narrowing abruptly forwards to the base of the mandibles, broadly rounded behind, with few hairs. Labrum reaching or almost reaching the apices of the mandibles. Antennae 16-segmented; segment 3 almost always shorter than segment 2, very rarely equal; segment 4 equal to or shorter than segment 3. Pronotum similar in shape to the large form. Measurements (large form / small form): total length 5.50—7.00 / 3.50—4.50; head length (including mandibles) 2.38—2.96 / 1.46—1.80; head length (to posterior margin of fontanelle) 1.28—1.59 / 0.80—0.92; head width 1.72—1.85 / 0.88—0.96; gula width at the narrowest point 0.36—0.40 / 0.27—0.29; pronotum length 0.55—0.62 / 0.40—0.44; pronotum width 1.21—1.33 / 0.70—0.77.

note: Rewritten from the English species-level description in Hill (1942). In the heading line the specific epithet was OCRed as "intermedins", an error for intermedius. The synonymy list (more than ten references from 1865—1933) is not translated entry by entry; the original does not describe the worker here, so no worker section is provided. The pronotum length of the alate is defective in the OCR and only the legible part is transcribed.
